Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh + 40 fps lock is the sweet spot for Dota 2 on Deck — smooth and stable through most team fights while keeping the APU well within its thermal budget. Medium textures and effects keep the game looking good without stressing the GPU.

profiles.Summary: Dota 2 is a well-optimized, older Valve title that runs natively on Linux and comfortably exceeds the Steam Deck's minimum requirements, making it a solid performer on the hardware. Expect stable 60 fps in most game states, with potential dips during large team fights at higher settings.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from Dota 2's PC minimum requirements, its Source 2 engine characteristics, and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU — which comfortably exceeds the minimum GPU spec. On your first run, check frame rates during a busy teamfight and adjust the TDP or settings tier accordingly.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render quality is dropped to 50% in-game and paired with FSR upscaling on the Deck side for maximum efficiency. TDP and GPU clock are capped low; Dota 2 is CPU-bound during fights, so this profile keeps thermals and draw very low for long sessions.

KnownIssues: No native Linux build; runs via Proton, though Gold/Platinum ProtonDB reports suggest it works well overall.
Occasional stutters or frame dips during large team fights (5v5 with heavy spell effects).
Steam Deck's on-screen keyboard may be needed for chat; a USB keyboard or the Steam virtual keyboard is recommended.
Anti-cheat (VAC) is active — ensure Proton compatibility is set correctly to avoid matchmaking issues.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Dota 2 is lightweight enough that native 1280x800 at high settings holds near-60 fps during most of the game; expect brief dips to 45-50 fps in the heaviest 5v5 teamfights. Ambient Occlusion is left off as it has the highest cost-to-benefit ratio in this engine.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at a stable 60 fps with a good-looking medium-high preset; the GPU auto-clock handles the light workload efficiently and leaves thermal headroom.

profiles.Summary: Dota 2 is a well-optimised, older (2013) Valve title that runs natively on Linux and performs well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps at medium-to-high settings. The game's ProtonDB gold rating and Playable Deck status reflect minor issues (likely controller/UI quirks) rather than any fundamental performance problem.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from Dota 2's 2013 vintage, its well-known Vulkan/Linux-native support, its modest PC minimum requirements (similar to GTX 8600/HD2600 class), and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU. On first launch, check frame rates during a busy team fight and adjust Shadow Quality and Ambient Occlusion first if performance dips.

MaxBattery.Notes: Renders at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to 1280x800 and a locked 40 fps/40 Hz to maximise battery life; Vulkan is preferred for lower CPU overhead on Linux.

KnownIssues: Controller/gamepad support is limited — the game is designed for mouse and keyboard, so a custom controller layout or touchpad use is recommended.
The in-game text and HUD can be small at 1280x800, requiring UI scale adjustments.
Occasional Proton-related shader compilation stutters on first launch may cause brief frame drops.
Anti-cheat (VAC) is active; ensure Proton compatibility is not interfering with VAC before playing ranked.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Targeting the OLED's 90 Hz ceiling with full GPU clock and no TDP cap; Dota 2 is light enough that the Deck can sustain this, though team-fight particle effects may briefly dip to the high-60s.
